text: You start a new game, eager to progress. It's thrilling: easy wins, constant momentum. You just want to keep going, to see what's next.
Then, everything slows. An impossible boss, or rare items needed. You're stuck, forced to replay old levels, or just wait for timers.
It feels unfair, bad design. Are they trying to annoy you? Perhaps it's a trick to make you spend money. You're frustrated, tempted to quit.
This isn't accidental. It's a precisely engineered system. Creating friction stretches the experience, giving just enough challenge to stay deeply engaged.
The cost? Your time, attention, and a subtle value shift. These pauses make future progress feel even more rewarding, deepening the addictive loop.
Next time you're stuck, you'll still want to progress. But now, you'll see invisible gears, knowing this "wait" is a feature, designed to keep you playing.
